reason: The quote states comprehensive BYOL support with existing per-socket, per-core or per-VM licenses including Windows Server, SQL Server, SLES and RHEL, subject to your license terms.

The claim gives one-year or three-year terms for all three payment options, but the context under 'Dedicated Host Reservations' says only some instance families support the three-year term for No Upfront; that condition is dropped. On-Demand, reservations with a billing discount, All Upfront as lowest effective price and Savings Plans for Dedicated Hosts are supported.
The quotes state a physical server fully dedicated for your use, optional sharing of instance capacity with other accounts, and visibility and control over placement with host affinity.
The decision-guide quote states Dedicated Hosts are priced per physical host rather than per instance and cost efficiency depends on how fully the instance capacity is used.
The quotes state a reservation covers one or more hosts of the same family in a single AZ, applies to the family not the size, and a host with a reservation can't be released until the term is over.
The table row 'Visibility of sockets, cores, and host ID' gives Dedicated Host: provides visibility of the number of sockets and physical cores; Dedicated Instance: No visibility.
The Billing row of the comparison table gives Per-host billing for Dedicated Host and Per-instance billing for Dedicated Instance.
The quote states both launch instances onto dedicated physical servers and there are no performance, security or physical differences between them.
Under 'Dedicated Instances limitations' the quote states the EBS volume of an EBS-backed Dedicated Instance doesn't run on single-tenant hardware.
The quote states hardware dedicated to a single account, physical isolation from other accounts even under one payer account, and possible sharing with non-dedicated instances of the same account.
The quote states no visibility or control over placement, no host affinity, a stop and start might move it to another host, and limited BYOL support.

The quotes state a default-tenancy RI applies only to default-tenancy running instances, not dedicated ones, and the modification process can't change RI tenancy; the Convertible exchange exception is in the qualifiers.
The quote states all families except T support Dedicated Spot Instances and only the largest or metal size of each supported family does.
The quote states that by default instances run on shared tenancy hardware and multiple accounts might share the same physical hardware.
The quote states each EBS volume has the DeleteOnTermination attribute and the default deletes the root volume and preserves other EBS volumes.
The quotes state the AMI determines the root volume type and AWS recommends EBS-backed AMIs because they launch faster and use persistent storage.
The pricing-page quote states EBS optimization is enabled by default at no additional cost for current generation instance types.

The quotes, read with the sentence about the stopped state between them, state stop and restart without affecting attached-volume data, and changing size or attaching the root volume to another running instance for debugging.
The quote states EFA is a network device you can attach to an EC2 instance to accelerate AI, ML and HPC applications.
The claim repeats the quote: lower and more consistent latency and higher throughput than the TCP transport of cloud HPC systems.
Under 'EFA pricing' the quote states EFA is an optional networking feature you can enable on any supported instance at no additional cost.
The quote states the Libfabric API bypasses the OS kernel and communicates directly with the EFA device, which reduces overhead.
Under 'EFA limitations' the quote states EFA traffic can't cross AZs or VPCs and that this does not apply to normal IP traffic from the ENA device.
The quote states the EFA device provides built-in OS-bypass and congestion control through SRD while the ENA device offers traditional IP networking.
The claim repeats the quote under 'Pricing'; it makes no statement about data transfer, so the separate cross-AZ data transfer charge in context does not contradict it.

The quotes state secure connection from the internet without a bastion host, without direct VPC internet connectivity, and without a public IPv4 or IPv6 address on the instance; the context names the internet gateway.
The quota row 'Maximum number of EC2 Instance Connect Endpoints per VPC' gives Default 1 and Adjustable No.
The quota row 'Maximum number of concurrent connections per EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint' gives Default 20 and Adjustable No.
The quota row 'Maximum number of EC2 Instance Connect Endpoints per AWS account per AWS Region' gives Default 5 and Adjustable No.
The quotes state a charge for all Elastic IP addresses in use or idle and that AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses including those on running instances.
The quotes state you can disassociate an Elastic IP and associate it with a different resource, and a disassociated address remains allocated until explicitly released.
The quote states an Elastic IP is a static IPv4 address and rapid remapping to another instance in your account masks instance or software failure.
The quotes state use in a specific Region only, no move to another Region, and no Elastic IPs for IPv6; 'static' is the list item directly above in context.
The quota row 'EC2-VPC Elastic IPs' gives Default 5, Adjustable Yes, described as the maximum number you can allocate in this Region.
The quote states higher bandwidth, higher PPS performance, consistently lower latency between instances, and no additional charge.
The quote states attachment to instances in the same AZ, attributes follow the interface on detach and reattach, and traffic is redirected to the new instance.
The quotes state a secondary ENI from a different VPC is allowed when in the same AZ as the instance, and multi-homed instances across VPCs in different accounts are not possible.

Under 'Low-budget, high-availability solution' the quotes state attaching the failed instance's interface to a hot standby; it keeps private IPs, Elastic IPs and MAC, traffic flows on attach, and no route table or DNS changes are needed.
The quote states each instance has a default primary network interface that you can't detach.
The quote states accelerated computing instances use hardware accelerators or co-processors for floating point, graphics or pattern matching more efficiently than software on CPUs.
